notes:
AE summary: mid-market product analytics SaaS. Started on Hosted API (sandbox) Oct-Nov 2025 for embeddings + search; moved to 2-week Dedicated POC in Feb 2026 to validate latency and cost at scale. POC environment deployed in us-east-1 VPC peering with customer network. Key ask: predictable monthly cost for product feature powering search + support bot; want burst for seasonal spikes and clear overage terms.

POC highlights:
- Workloads tested: batch embeddings ingestion (~300k docs/day, 512-dim), interactive support-agent chat (~1k DAU), reranking candidate set (top-50).
- Latency targets: p50 <50ms for embeddings, p99 target <=150ms for chat/rerank. POC achieved p50 40ms, p95 110ms, p99 210ms under 4x synthetic load — need kernel/placement tuning to hit p99 SLA.
- Throughput observed: sustained 120 requests/sec for rerank during stress window (with batching enabled).
- Cost telemetry: hosted baseline was ~30% higher per-token; Dedicated POC showed potential savings of 35-45% with caching + quantized model variant.
- Security: SOC2 + SAML demo acceptable; need explicit KMS integration and audit log export to customer's Splunk.

Pricing / packaging discussion notes:
- Cypress Grove requests 12-month reserved commitment with 3-month ramp (50% commit first month, 75% second, 100% third).
- Proposed reserved capacity: equivalent of 2 x V100-class GPUs baseline (expect to map to Redwood Dedicated SKU: r-dedicated-2) with optional burst +2 GPUs for up to 6 hours/day during business hours.
- Commit metric debated: tokens/day vs reserved GPU-hours. Customer prefers predictable token-based commit because their billing/product metrics align to tokens. AE suggests hybrid: reserved token bundle convertible to GPU-hours for scheduling.
- Overage: customer wants a soft cap and auto-burst; Redwood proposed overage at 1.5x list hosted rate after reserved consumption. Customer pushed for 1.25x for first 90 days of ramp.
- Ramp credits: Cypress Grove asked for ramp discount (30% off overage rates) first 60 days; Redwood offered staging credits and 2 weeks free burst to validate go-live.
- Term/exit: 12-mo contract with quarterly business review; early termination fee if cancel before 6 months. Customer legal pushing softer termination terms.

Recent timeline (bulleted):
- 2025-10-12: Hosted API sandbox onboarding, basic embeddings POC
- 2025-11-20: Internal spike test showed cost concerns with hosted at high ingestion rates
- 2026-01-14: Intro demo with Jordan (AE) + Maya (SE) — showed Dedicated capabilities
- 2026-02-02: Security questionnaire submitted (SSO + SOC2 + KMS questions)
- 2026-02-18: Fireflies call — scope for Dedicated POC; agreed to VPC peering and test dataset
- 2026-03-01 to 2026-03-05: 2-week Dedicated POC in us-east-1 — stress + latency validation (see POC results above)
- 2026-03-08: Pricing call with procurement — attempted to align commit metric to tokens; legal raised residency clause

Sales/tech notes (shorthand):
- SE feedback: need kernel/kvs tuning; examine smaller context-window model variant for p99 improvements. Try compression/quant quantization profiles.
- Product ask: can Redwood expose burst scheduling UI and projected overage estimator in Console for finance sign-off?
- AE ask: pricing term to include clear ramp schedule + trial credits; final proposal due by 2026-03-20.

Customer quote snippets: "If we can hit p99 <150ms and a predictable cost with burst built-in, we can put this in our Q2 roadmap and commit to a year deal." — Head of Platform (email 2026-03-03).
